```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# --- Setup chunk ------------------------------------------------
# include = FALSE runs this code but hides it (and its output) in the report

# echo = FALSE hides the code in every chunk by default, so readers see
# results, not code; change to TRUE if you want the code to show
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)

# Load packages
library(tidyverse)    # dplyr, ggplot2, readr
library(moderndive)   # get_regression_table(), get_regression_summaries(), get_correlation()
library(knitr)        # kable() turns a table into a neat report table
library(here)         # here() builds file paths from the project folder

# This file lives in reports/, but our data and outputs are one folder up.
# here() finds the project folder (the one holding the .Rproj file), so
# the same paths work whichever folder the .Rmd is in.
# Load the cleaned data and the saved final model from our scripts
heart       <- readRDS(here("data", "clean", "heart_clean.rds"))
model_final <- readRDS(here("outputs", "models", "final.rds"))
```

# Exploratory analysis

<!-- WRITE: The distribution of the outcome (mean, median, SD, Q-Q plot) and
     of the predictors. The size of each category group. -->

```{r outcome-summary}
# summarise() collapses the data to one row of statistics for the outcome
heart |>
  summarise(n      = n(),
            mean   = mean(resting_bp_systolic),
            median = median(resting_bp_systolic),
            sd     = sd(resting_bp_systolic),
            min    = min(resting_bp_systolic),
            max    = max(resting_bp_systolic)) |>
  kable(digits = 1, caption = "Resting systolic BP (mmHg)")
```

```{r outcome-plots}
# include_graphics() inserts a plot saved earlier by ggsave()
include_graphics(here("outputs", "plots", "outcome_histogram.png"))
include_graphics(here("outputs", "plots", "outcome_qq.png"))
```

<!-- WRITE: One sentence under each plot saying what the reader should notice. -->

```{r categories}
# count() tallies each category; mutate() adds the percentage
heart |>
  count(smoker_status) |>
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
  kable(caption = "Smoking status")
```

# Models

## Simple regression (age only)

<!-- WRITE: The age slope in everyday words, with its 95% CI, and R-squared. -->

```{r simple-model}
# Refit the simple model; get_regression_table() gives estimates and 95% CIs
model_age <- lm(resting_bp_systolic ~ age, data = heart)

get_regression_table(model_age, digits = 3) |>
  kable(caption = "Simple regression: systolic BP and age")
```

## Multiple regression and variable selection

<!-- WRITE: Which variables you added, which you dropped and WHY
     (confidence intervals including 0, the anova() p-value, overlap
     between steps and exercise). -->

## Final model

<!-- WRITE: The final model formula and why you chose it. -->

```{r final-model}
# Coefficient table for the final model
get_regression_table(model_final, digits = 3) |>
  kable(caption = "Final model: coefficients and 95% confidence intervals")

# Overall fit: R-squared, adjusted R-squared, RMSE
get_regression_summaries(model_final) |>
  select(r_squared, adj_r_squared, rmse, nobs) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Final model fit")
```
